baseline.scope: inner-face-only; physical enclosure owns the cat silhouette

iterations.prompt: Create a pure black-and-white 1-bit reference sheet for a premium Companion internal-face expression system on a 200x200 e-paper display. Use the accepted generated_pet_expression_sheet_v5 inner-face aesthetic as the strict baseline: rounded refined eyes, brows, lids, tiny nose and mouth, subtle cheeks, and very sparse state marks. The physical enclosure supplies the cat outline, so draw no ears, head contour, whiskers, body, device frame, text, border, gray, color, or gradient. Show seven separate, highly legible state cells: low-power sleep, touch wake, tap acknowledgement, directional swipe response, recording starts, active recording, and recording saved or failed. Each state must alter the complete face rather than only the eyes. Make low-power calm and static-looking; make recording alert but not noisy; retain large white space and stroke weights that survive 1-bit conversion to 200x200.

review.reason: Touch interrupt and Stop-wake hardware evidence has priority.

iterations.prompt: Create a pure black-and-white 1-bit storyboard reference sheet for a premium Companion internal-face expression system on a 200x200 e-paper display. Strictly preserve the accepted generated_pet_expression_sheet_v5 aesthetic: refined rounded black eyes, expressive brows and lids, tiny nose and mouth, gentle cheek shapes, and sparse black state marks. The device enclosure supplies the cat outline, so draw no ears, head contour, whiskers, body, device frame, text, labels, borders, gray, color, or gradients. Use a clean 4-column by 3-row equal-cell grid with one large face centered in each cell. The sheet must make these states immediately recognizable at a glance: row 1: 1 deep low-power sleep with completely closed soft eyelids, relaxed tiny mouth, low drooping brows, two small Z sleep marks, and a calm cheek shape; 2 sleep breathing-in with the same closed sleepy face and slightly fuller cheeks; 3 sleep breathing-out with the same closed sleepy face and slightly relaxed cheeks; 4 touch wake with lids lifting, alert round pupils, raised brows, and one small wake sparkle. Row 2: 5 recording starts with focused open eyes, listening brows, a small open mouth, and tiny sound dots; 6 active recording keyframe A with intent pupils, listening brows, cheeks lifted, and curved sound marks on both sides; 7 active recording keyframe B with a soft blink, changed mouth and cheeks, and a different pair of side sound marks; 8 active recording keyframe C with eyes wide again, changed brow angle and open listening mouth, and a third side sound rhythm. Row 3: 9 second-double-tap stop or saving with eyes gently closing, pursed concentrating mouth, and two compact saving dots; 10 recording saved with relieved happy closed eyes, smiling mouth, raised cheeks, and one small sparkle; 11 recording failed or retry with uncertain asymmetrical lids, tiny concerned mouth, and one compact retry mark; 12 quiet idle recovery with open calm eyes and neutral relaxed mouth. Every cell must change the complete inner face, not only the eyes. The recording A/B/C sequence must visibly feel alive and continuous through coordinated eyes, lids, brows, mouth, cheeks, and side sound marks, but it must remain low-frequency-keyframe friendly for e-paper. Use large white space and bold clean strokes that survive 1-bit conversion at 200x200.
source_references: COMP-REQ-009 obvious low-power sleep and dynamic recording visual acceptance
